The ending feels entirely natural and earned because it provides full thematic and emotional closure. Throughout the story, the narrator wrestles with the myth of Q's inhuman perfection and his own feelings of inadequacy in comparison. The climax at the pool shatters this myth, allowing the narrator to finally see Q's vulnerability and human friction. The conclusion thoughtfully ties together the motifs established at the very beginning of the story—the Marcus Aurelius index cards, the frittatas, and the visual metaphor of the letter "Q" with its "little tail flicking off somewhere private"—showing how this secret observation has fundamentally shifted the narrator's perspective and brought him a quiet sense of peace in his own imperfect life.
